clue.text: Notice in broken-down cafe's frontage

indicators.note: in tells us the notice sits inside the rearranged letters
something broken down has fallen apart, so the letters of cafe are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
a notice in a paper can be an advertisement, an AD

explanation.surface: A dilapidated café has a sign posted on its shopfront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb but gives the advert; 'broken-down' rearranges the cafe and 'in' sets the advert inside, after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A façade is the front face of a building, its frontage onto the street.

clue.text: Predict the account will turn up in Epping, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the turned account inside the woodland

parts.note: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the edge of London, so Epping is an example of a forest

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading the letters backwards from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone predicts their bank statement will surface in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'will turn up' reads the account backwards from below, and 'in' sets it inside the woodland. Epping is a town in Essex beside Epping Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to estimate in advance what will happen, as a weather forecaster predicts rain.

clue.text: No coy chap involved in discord?

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who is not shy is caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh clash of sounds is discord in the musical sense.

clue.text: Record to become aware of? Not half

indicators.note: not half means the second half of the word is dropped

parts.note: to discover something is to become aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone notices a record only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' cuts DISCOVER to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat circular disc.

clue.text: Wearing coat (mufti) endlessly I do various jobs

indicators.note: wearing in the sense of wearing down or fraying, so the letters are worked into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of mufti is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone in casual clothes and a coat claims to take on all sorts of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MUFTI to MUFT; 'Wearing' then rearranges COAT plus MUFT. MUFTI is civilian dress worn by someone normally in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or handyman employed to do every kind of task; the clue speaks in the first person.

clue.text: Speech gets publicity cover age

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Speech gets publicity cover age (7)': AD (publicity) + DRESS (cover) gives ADDRESS, but 'age' gives no letters and is no link word; the clue appears garbled in OCR and no source found.

clue.text: It's produced by a certain brand

definitions.text: It's produced by a certain brand

parts.words: It's produced by a certain brand
parts.note: brand reads as a commercial label but also means a burning stick carried for light

explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a flaming piece of wood, a torch, and the glow it gives is the light from a torch.

clue.text: Country's capital in real ceasefire

indicators.note: in places the capital letter inside the word for real

parts.note: real means true

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so take the opening letter of country

explanation.surface: A nation's capital is the scene of a genuine ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' gives C, the first letter of Country, and 'in' puts it inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreed halt to fighting, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Two ways to become unassuming

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way or road

explanation.surface: Advice on two methods of becoming humble.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person is humble and not inclined to boast.

clue.text: Failure of fielder at college

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A cricketer who plays at university fails.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand behind the batter, close to the wicketkeeper, to catch edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a careless mistake or lapse.

clue.text: Unwavering kind of music sound

parts.note: rock is a genre of popular music
sound in the sense of solid, firm and reliable

explanation.surface: A musician's genre is described as steady and having a strong sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely firm and dependable does not waver.

clue.text: Approximate number of drinks for a group

definitions.text: number of drinks for a group

explanation.definitionFit: To approximate a figure is to make it whole without fractions, and a set of drinks bought for everyone in a party is the same word.

clue.text: Deal successfully with ceremonial cloak

explanation.definitionFit: To manage a difficulty is to handle it successfully; a long semicircular vestment worn by clergy on ceremonial occasions shares the spelling.

clue.text: One could be this if stunned

definitions.text: One could be this if stunned

parts.words: One could be this if stunned
parts.note: a person struck dumb with astonishment is left with nothing to say

explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned can leave someone unable to utter a word, at a loss for anything to say.

clue.text: Ag-surfeit's taken in repeatedly. Antibody required

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a surfeit is a glut

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word in is used twice

explanation.surface: Too much silver is swallowed over and over and a medicine is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglutinin is an antibody that makes particles such as bacteria clump together.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory pots break You'll need a substitute

indicators.note: unsatisfactory pots are not right as they stand, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: a break is a gap or interval

explanation.surface: A potter whose pots have cracked is told a replacement will be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsatisfactory' is the anagram signal on the pots; 'You'll need a' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary replacement filling a gap until something better arrives is a substitute.

clue.text: A particular wind left Paris in trouble

indicators.note: a city in trouble is in disorder, so the letters of Paris are rearranged

explanation.surface: A certain breeze departs from a troubled French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges the city. 'wind' rhymes with 'kind' here, a winding or twist, not a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral is one specific kind of winding curve, coiling round a centre.

clue.text: Umpire's air batter disturbed

definitions.note: umpire is the verb, and the 's stands for is, linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An umpire's airing complaint upsets the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute impartially, as an umpire decides a game.

clue.text: Pets made mad rush

indicators.note: mad means wildly disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frenzied animals hurtle about.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of a panicked crowd or herd.

clue.text: Recurring series of changes seen in Tour de France

explanation.definitionFit: Periodic sequences that repeat are called by this name, and bicycles ridden in the great French race are too.

clue.text: Rescue learner in attack

indicators.note: in places the learner inside the word for attack

parts.note: to savage is to attack fiercely
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A novice driver is rescued from an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to save something from loss or wreckage.

clue.text: Become inmate in hospital a short time

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a short time is a bit, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: A patient is admitted to hospital for a brief stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell in a place is to become one of its occupants or residents.

clue.text: Remove top from coal in fire

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: lignite is a soft brown coal

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear the upper coal from a grate.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, kindle it.

clue.text: Mop lab after accident showing composure

indicators.note: after an accident things are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone calmly cleans the laboratory after a spill.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and calm under pressure.

clue.text: Indicate centre of target directly

parts.note: to indicate something is to point to it
the blank is the white spot at the centre of an archery target

explanation.surface: An archer gestures at the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something bluntly, without hedging, is saying it straight out and directly.

clue.text: The cake's topping!

parts.note: read as the sugary layer spread over a cake

explanation.definitionFit: The sweet glaze covering a cake is its sugary coating, and the phrase means a final extra bonus.

clue.text: Some favourite mistakes occurring in article

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is full of a writer's pet errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'occurring in', but those words are the link; 'article' alone means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An article in a newspaper, or a single object in a list, is called a piece or entry of that name.

clue.text: Unsecured on the house?

explanation.definitionFit: Something unfastened is loose and unrestrained, and on the house means given at no charge.

clue.text: Working on backing number one vegetable?

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on

indicators.note: backing means the following pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A farm hand is keen on his first-choice vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses number plus one together. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb with pungent layers is a common kitchen vegetable.

clue.text: Every second bird in an unusual tale?

indicators.note: in puts the bird inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A

indicators.note: an unusual tale is told differently, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A strange story features a bird in every other line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges only the tale, giving LATE after A; 'in' then sets the seabird inside, after AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on each other occasion, skipping one each time, is doing it every second time.

clue.text: Henry's heart being in turmoil as a novice

indicators.note: in turmoil means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle, everything but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Henry is emotionally troubled as a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of Henry is ENR; 'in turmoil' rearranges ENR with BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a learner, someone just starting out at something.

clue.text: Retire: about to get the pip, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: a pip is a seed, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A retiree is told they are about to get the pip, in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'get the pip' is British slang for being annoyed, which misleads; here the pip is a fruit seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to withdraw or move back, which is what retiring from a position means.
